deviations.what: t10 proof dispatches run codex with --sandbox danger-full-access instead of the plan's workspace-write: codex's own workspace-write sandbox denies network regardless of the account (the exact #230 failure), and --handover only mints a local ref on a fresh workspace-write session and never pushes (preserve.py:569-660), so the proof's fetch + push can only happen when nothing but the account confines the session. Under #243 that is the design: the account IS the fence. The bridge argv is unchanged (c15); only the dispatch option differs. README's old rejection of danger-full-access was under the shared-login-user model and is superseded by the deviation record (t6).

deviations.what: t10 proof: the spec's 'commit and push its handover ref' (c9/h9/c23) is replaced by the repo's own actor rule (AGENTS.md: never git push from a session, never commit onto a branch; the write path is a handover ref under refs/culture-nodes/<run-id>). The proof therefore runs --sandbox workspace-write --handover with network enabled in the ACCOUNT's codex config ([sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = true, rendered by lanes/unix-user.sh), and the operator fetches the ref as the account: git fetch culture-codex@<host>:git/culture-nodes-agent refs/culture-nodes/<run-id>. d1's danger-full-access dispatches proved network, formatters, loopback and denials (runs 01M17E36Z7G8A60WP6TA9QB0AP, 01M17E3ZC1MBQ6DZRKY93T8PWE) and are kept as evidence; the write-path leg runs under this posture instead.
